cluster.headline: US sanctions 36 targets over Iran aviation under Operation Economic Outcast
cluster.summary: The US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned 36 targets under Operation Economic Outcast, framed by the State Department as entities and individuals in multiple jurisdictions aiding Iran's aviation sector, covering more than two dozen commercial and private airlines plus foreign cargo providers, including Air Shiraz, Fly Persia, Fly Kish, Ata, Ava and Chabahar Airlines. Treasury warned firms enabling sanctioned carriers through aircraft transfers, cargo services or general sales agent support are exposed, and a general licence for reexporting certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn is listed as suspended as of September 8, 2026.

story.headline: US Treasury sanctions 36 targets over support to Iran's aviation sector
story.body:
The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has designated 36 targets under an action described as Operation Economic Outcast, according to the intake note prepared from Treasury and State Department releases and the OFAC website. The State Department has framed the targets as entities and individuals across multiple jurisdictions that assist Iran's aviation sector.

The designations are said to cover more than two dozen commercial and private airlines along with foreign cargo providers. Carriers named in the intake material include Air Shiraz, Fly Persia, Fly Kish, Ata, Ava and Chabahar Airlines. The desk has not independently verified the full target list against the OFAC entry.

Treasury also issued a warning that companies enabling sanctioned carriers — through aircraft transfers, cargo services or general sales agent support — face exposure to sanctions themselves, per the same releases. The precise wording and scope of that warning still needs to be read off the primary Treasury document.

The intake note further records that a general licence permitting the reexport of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn is listed as suspended as of September 8, 2026. The licence number, the reason given for the suspension and whether the suspension is time-limited are not stated in the material available.

Bloomberg, Al Jazeera and NOTUS are listed as having picked up the story, but no wire copy from those outlets has reached the desk, and none of their reporting is reflected here. No Iranian government response has been recorded in the material at hand.

Before publication the desk must confirm: the OFAC press release and Specially Designated Nationals list entries for all 36 targets and the exact spelling of each airline; whether "Operation Economic Outcast" is Treasury's own label or the State Department's; the identity of the non-Iranian jurisdictions and cargo providers involved; the general licence number and the accuracy of the September 8, 2026 suspension date, which should be checked as it may be a transcription error; the direct language of Treasury's secondary-exposure warning; and any response from Tehran or from the named carriers.

blocks.label: Blurb
lines: The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has designated 36 targets under an action described as Operation Economic Outcast, which the State Department has framed as aimed at those assisting Iran's aviation sector.

The designations are said to cover more than two dozen airlines, with Air Shiraz, Fly Persia, Fly Kish, Ata, Ava and Chabahar Airlines among the carriers named, while Treasury has also warned that companies enabling sanctioned carriers face exposure to sanctions themselves.
A general licence for the reexport of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn is listed as suspended as of September 8, 2026, and no Iranian government response has been recorded.
Our note sets out what the releases state so far, and what the desk has yet to confirm.

blocks.label: Intro
lines: The United States has hit Iran's aviation sector with a fresh round of sanctions.
The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has designated 36 targets.

blocks.label: Body
lines: The action is described as Operation Economic Outcast.
The State Department frames the targets as entities and individuals that assist Iran's aviation sector.
The designations cover more than two dozen airlines. Named carriers include Air Shiraz, Fly Persia, Fly Kish, Ata, Ava and Chabahar Airlines.
Treasury also warned that companies enabling sanctioned carriers face exposure to sanctions themselves.
And a general licence for the reexport of certain civil aircraft to Iran is listed as suspended, as of September the eighth, 2026.

blocks.label: Outro
lines: No Iranian government response has been recorded so far.
Bloomberg, Al Jazeera and NOTUS are listed as having picked up the story.

brief.headline: US Treasury sanctions 36 targets over support to Iran's aviation sector
brief.body:
The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control has designated 36 targets under an action described as Operation Economic Outcast, according to the intake note prepared from Treasury and State Department releases and the OFAC website. The State Department has framed the targets as entities and individuals across multiple jurisdictions that assist Iran's aviation sector.

The designations are said to cover more than two dozen commercial and private airlines along with foreign cargo providers. Carriers named in the intake material include Air Shiraz, Fly Persia, Fly Kish, Ata, Ava and Chabahar Airlines. The desk has not independently verified the full target list against the OFAC entry.

Treasury also issued a warning that companies enabling sanctioned carriers — through aircraft transfers, cargo services or general sales agent support — face exposure to sanctions themselves, per the same releases. The precise wording and scope of that warning still needs to be read off the primary Treasury document.

The intake note further records that a general licence permitting the reexport of certain civil aircraft to Iran on temporary sojourn is listed as suspended as of September 8, 2026. The licence number, the reason given for the suspension and whether the suspension is time-limited are not stated in the material available.

Bloomberg, Al Jazeera and NOTUS are listed as having picked up the story, but no wire copy from those outlets has reached the desk, and none of their reporting is reflected here. No Iranian government response has been recorded in the material at hand.

Before publication the desk must confirm: the OFAC press release and Specially Designated Nationals list entries for all 36 targets and the exact spelling of each airline; whether "Operation Economic Outcast" is Treasury's own label or the State Department's; the identity of the non-Iranian jurisdictions and cargo providers involved; the general licence number and the accuracy of the September 8, 2026 suspension date, which should be checked as it may be a transcription error; the direct language of Treasury's secondary-exposure warning; and any response from Tehran or from the named carriers.
